link.note: Probable (~80%). Her marriage to John Tuthill at Smithtown on 23 Nov 1752 is proved by the church register (NYGBR 44:283), which does not name her father. Five compilers list a Temperance among the children of James Smith & Jerusha Topping (Thompson 1843, Weygant 1897, Pelletreau 1898, Reynolds 1914, F. K. Smith 1967); F. K. Smith adds that she was 'supposed to have m. John Tuthill, brother of above Mehitable', the wife of her brother Austin. Her brothers Austin and Francis were at Woodbury Clove by about 1755, where Keturah was born. The other Smithtown Temperances (Ebenezer's daughter, Mrs Jonas Platt, married Feb 1752; Job 2d's daughter, b. 1714) do not fit, and every candidate is a Bull Smith descendant.

birth.place: Moriches, Brookhaven, Suffolk County, New York, USA

summary: Daughter of James Smith of Moriches and great-granddaughter of Bull Smith, wife of John Tuthill and mother of Keturah Tuttle; John's 7th-great-grandmother.
bio:
Temperance Smith was born about 1735 at Moriches, Brookhaven, Suffolk County, New York, probably the daughter of James Smith, who settled at Moriches, and Jerusha Topping, daughter of the younger Elnathan Topping (1664–1751). Through James she was a granddaughter of Job Smith and a great-granddaughter of Richard Bull Smith, the founder of Smithtown. Two early printed genealogies list her among the children of James and Jerusha, with Matthew, born in 1721, Ezekiel, Zebulon, Austin, Nathaniel, Francis, Eunice, Keturah and Jeremiah; as one of the youngest she fits a birth about 1732 to 1735.

On 23 November 1752 she married John Tuthill in the Presbyterian church at Smithtown, and was known thereafter as Temperance Tuttle. Her brother Zebulon had married there in March of the same year, and her brother Austin married John's sister Mehitable. By 1755 the couple were living at Woodbury Clove in Orange County. She named her eldest known daughter Keturah after her sister and a son Ezekiel after her brother, and Keturah in turn named her children James, Temperance and Keturah. In 1775 and 1776 two of her brothers, Captain Francis Smith and Captain Austin Smith, commanded the Woodbury Clove and Upper Clove militia companies in Orange County, with her son-in-law Thomas Lamoreaux serving as ensign under Francis. She died about 1780 in Orange County, New York.

Temperance is the link that carries the whole Smith, Thompson, Topping, Hammond and Paine ancestry down to John, who is her 7th-great-grandson. The church register proves the wedding but does not name the bride's father. A twentieth-century history of the Smith family says she was "supposed" to have married John Tuthill, the brother of her brother Austin's wife, and the double marriage, the militia companies and the family names all point the same way. She is not to be confused with her first cousin Temperance, daughter of Job Smith 2d, born in 1714 and too old to be the same woman, nor with the Temperance daughter of Ebenezer Smith who married Jonas Platt and died his widow in 1813.

researchNotes:
Temperance is the link that carries the whole Smith, Thompson, Topping, Hammond and Paine ancestry. Pelletreau's appendix (p. 479) says James Smith 'settled in Moriches' and married Jerusha Topping, and lists their children as Matthew (b. 1721), Ezekiel, Zebulon, Austin, Nathaniel, Francis, Eunice, Keturah, Temperance and Jeremiah. Temperance Tuttle named her eldest known daughter Keturah (after her sister) and a son Ezekiel (after her brother); Keturah in turn named children James (1774), Temperance (1778) and Keturah (1791). Two of her brothers, Capt. Francis Smith and Capt. Austin Smith, commanded the Woodbury Clove and Upper Clove militia companies in Orange County in 1775–76, with her son-in-law Thomas Lamoreaux as ensign under Francis. Earlier research had a rival candidate: Ebenezer Smith (son of Richard 2d) whose will of 25 Jul 1747 (proved 7 Jan 1747 O.S.; Pelletreau p. 46) left £100 each to 'my daughters Temperance Anna and Hannah' when 21, with wife Anna daughter of Job Smith 2d (p. 472). Pelletreau's appendix (pp. 465, 475) says twice that this Temperance married Jonas Platt and died 12 Mar 1813 his widow, so she cannot be Mrs. Tuttle; that candidacy is closed. Job Smith 2d's daughter Temperance (b. 1714) is about 20 years too early. A chronology question was raised (Jerusha's father 'died in 1705') and resolved in Round 1: Jerusha's father was the younger Elnathan Topping (1664–1751), not Capt. Elnathan (d. 1705). No grave found. A full-text search of Pelletreau found no Tuthill/Tuttle tied to her.

Temperance is now named as a daughter of James Smith & Jerusha Topping of Moriches in two independent printed genealogies that predate Alva Tuttle (1968). Pelletreau (1898) lists the children as Matthew (b. 3 Sept 1721), Ezekiel, Zebulon, Austin, Nathaniel, Francis, Eunice, Keturah, Temperance and Jeremiah ([R4-S1]). C. H. Weygant's Family Record (1897), written for the Weygant family, who married into Capt. Francis Smith's line, lists nine children: Nathan [sic, for Matthew], Ezekiel, Austin, Nathaniel, Francis, Eunice, Keturah, Temperance and Jerusha ([R4-S2]). Neither source names her husband, so the step 'this Temperance = Mrs. John Tuthill' still rests on Alva Tuttle and on circumstantial evidence. That evidence is the Woodbury Clove militia under her brothers and the naming of Keturah's children.

Two cautions. (1) Her first cousin, Temperance daughter of Job Smith 2d, was born 19 June 1714 ([R4-S1]). She is too old to be Mrs. Tuthill (m. 1752), but she is a likely source of confusion in online trees. (2) The eldest brother Matthew was born in 1721, so Temperance, as one of the youngest, fits a birth c.1732-35.

Nov 2026: the marriage is proved by Daggett's Smithtown register (NYGBR 44:283), on the same pages as Jonas Platt & Temperance Smith (Ebenezer's daughter, 10 Feb 1752) and Zebulon Smith & Elizabeth Green (26 Mar 1752). Thompson (1843, vol. 2 App. p. 453), the earliest printed list, already includes Temperance among James & Jerusha's children. F. K. Smith (1967) nos. 102 and 107: Austin m. Mehitable Tuthill; 'Temperance, supposed to have m. John Tuthill, brother of above Mehitable'. A Rock Smith family (Thomas Smith Sr., patent c.1732) also lived at Woodbury Clove, which is why the Smithtown wedding matters: it ties this Temperance to the Bull Smith family. No deed, will or church entry yet names Temperance Tuthill as James Smith's daughter; best targets are Suffolk deeds Libers C–G (a partition of James Smith's estate naming 'John Tuthill and Temperance his wife') and Austin Smith's Loyalist claim (AO 12/13).
